verdict.rationale: Greptile documents its own noise controls: a 1–3 strictness setting, comment-type filters, a noise-control mode that skips low-impact or repetitive feedback, learning from 👍/👎 reactions, a v5 engine that flags fewer false positives, and a findings list sorted by severity. One user says it is 'sometimes a bit overzealous' but usually catches real issues, which is mild sentiment rather than a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: explicit deduplication of comments (only 'repetitive feedback' skipping is documented), explicit per-comment severity labels rather than a severity-sorted summary list, independent measurement of the false-positive rate.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, the reviewer keeps noise low — few false positives, deduplicated comments, severity labels — so my team doesn't tune it out

citations.quote: With noise control, Greptile limits reviews to high-signal insights, skipping low impact or repetitive feedback.
Control how strict Greptile is about leaving comments with the strictness setting (1–3).
v5 is faster, catches more bugs, and flags fewer false positives by running a swarm of narrowly scoped agents in parallel.
A Findings list sorted by severity, with links to each comment.
After 2-3 weeks, it stops commenting on things you don't care about.
more often than not it catches real issues
